explanation: Right after saying he has "undergone a great deal," Trofimov lists hardships: he is hungry, ill, shaken, and tossed everywhere by fate. So "undergone" means lived through or endured something difficult. "Enjoyed" clashes with that list of suffering, and "neglected" or "conveyed" don't describe experiencing events.

Realism focuses on accurate, ordinary experience, while the romantic style exaggerated beauty and heroism and hid imperfection. A style built on the opposite principle would be an effort to counteract, or work against, those romantic excesses. "Accentuate" and "advance" would mean strengthening the excesses, and "understand" misses the opposition the text sets up.

explanation: The underlined sentence simply tells what the Hibulb Cultural Center does (presents Tulalip history and culture) and how (using traditional knowledge to design exhibits). That is a basic description of one center. It doesn't contrast it with other tribal centers; in fact the next sentence says the Comanche center is similar, so C is wrong.

fix.passage: In what is now Washington state, the Tulalip Tribes operate the Hibulb Cultural Center. <u>Relying on traditional knowledge to guide the design of exhibits, this institution presents Tulalip history and culture to the tribes' citizens.</u> The Comanche Nation, a tribe in Oklahoma, employs a similar strategy in its own cultural center. Both centers contrast with museums that aren't Indigenous-led; when displaying Indigenous artifacts, such museums tend to anticipate mainly non-Indigenous audiences and rely on Euro-centric strategies for designing exhibits.

If M. anniana spread beyond Tamaulipas, its range would widen, so a result "consistent with previous findings" would show its genetic homogeneity decreasing. The other choices shift the focus to other Mammillaria species, which the simulation of M. anniana's spread doesn't address.

explanation: The subject "Raymond Chang's textbook General Chemistry: The Essential Concepts" needs a main verb to make a complete sentence. "Discusses" is a finite present-tense verb that fits. "Discussing," "to discuss," and "having discussed" are not finite verbs, so they would leave the sentence a fragment.

The text states a general definition, and the next sentence also uses the present tense ("are commonly used"). The present-tense "serves" matches that and agrees with the singular "compound." The past forms "served," "had served," and "was serving" wrongly suggest something that only happened in the past.

The words after the blank, "the Hawai'i Register of Historic Places," name the important list mentioned before it. A colon is the right way to introduce that kind of specification after a complete clause. A period or semicolon would leave "the Hawai'i Register of Historic Places" as a fragment, and no punctuation runs the list and its name together.

Both "Brothers Andre and Edouard Michelin sought... restaurants" and "as it grew in scope and influence, the guide had its modest French eateries replaced..." are independent clauses. A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses. A comma alone creates a comma splice, and no punctuation or just "and" produces a run-on.

Brothers Andre and Edouard Michelin sought to increase profits for their tire company by encouraging their customers to drive across France, visiting the guide's recommended hotels and _____ as it grew in scope and influence, the guide had its modest French eateries replaced with the best restaurants from around the world, including The Eight in Macau and Sushi Ueda in Nagoya.

The underlined claim in Text 1 is that automated genre classification hasn't worked well and may be at its technological limit. Text 2 describes Costa's team solving a hard classification problem by turning sound into images, saying it shows "how much innovation is possible." So the Text 2 author would reply that these systems can still be improved. Neither text discusses listeners' disagreement or bias toward certain genres.

fix.passage:
Text 1
<u>Attempts to automate classification of music into genres have not been very successful, and we may be at the limit of what is technologically possible.</u> But it's not clear that this is a worthwhile pursuit in any case—as Jin Ha Lee and Anh Thu Nguyen argue in their study of the South Korean band BTS, relationships between pieces of music may be best understood with concepts other than genre.

Text 2
Tango is a genre of music originally from Argentina and Uruguay that shares some harmonic and rhythmic similarities with the pagode genre. Automated genre classification systems typically struggle to draw distinctions in situations like this, but Yandre Costa and colleagues solved that problem by converting sound to images and having computers compare features of those images, an approach that demonstrates how much innovation is possible in this field.
